Monitoring: Visually search for whiteflies one rice leaves twice a month
Adults are tiny (about 1 to 1.5 mm) white-winged insects.
When 3 to 8 whiteflies on average per each of 30 to 50 checked plants, then consider green control action
After green control, if whitefly numbers still increase up to 10 to 40 whiteflies on average per each of 30 to 50 checked plants, then consider green control action
Young and adult white flies suck rice leaf juice which will yellow, mottle, sometimes curl the leaves
Place 3 to 10 yellow sticky traps per field to track whiteflies at the beginning of the season, this is early
If 10 to 20 whiteflies are found per trap consider green control, and at 20 to 50 flies yellow control
Direct Control: Release 10000 natural enemies ( Encarsia wasp species) per acre at early occurrence of whiteflies.
Repeat 2 to 4 times every 5 to 7 days

Release predatory beetles ( Delphastus species) twice in two weeks
Restrictions: Most chemical sprays will kill the released biocontrol agents.
Apply chemicals as uniform flat spray reaching both sides of leaves (white flies are mainly undersides).
Do not spray at wind, or if raining within an hour.
When using a chemical or botanical pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
